atoms.a:
Knock gently on a hard surface like a table or wall. Think about how loud the sound is. Now knock again but harder than before.

How did the sound change?

feedback.end: The sound is louder because more force was used. The higher the force, the higher the energy that is transferred into the vibrations.

atoms.b: Louder sounds are created by ((++high low))-energy vibrations. The more ((++force luck)) put into making a sound, the louder it will be.
Quieter sounds are made by ((++low high))-energy vibrations. The less force put into making a sound, the ((++quieter louder)) it will be.

instruction.text: Harry hits the longest bar very gently, and the shortest bar much harder. Select the bar that will produce the quietest sound.

hint.text:
Loud sounds are produced by high-energy vibrations which are made from more forceful actions.

Quieter sounds are produced by lower-energy vibrations, which are made from lighter actions.

instruction.text: Why does this bar make the quietest sound?

feedback.end: The less force used, the quieter the sound will be.

instruction.text: Listen to what happens to the volume when Darla blows across the opening of bottles 1, 2 and 3. You can repeat the sounds as many times as you need.

atoms.a: Which bottle made the loudest sound?
Why might bottle 2 have made a louder sound?
Why would blowing harder increase the volume of the sound?
